scope: Selected mechanism-overlap and source-to-label risk queue across all public development families; not a claim that unlisted pairs are independent.

overlaps.reason: Both challenge treating a positive microbiology result without compatible symptoms. Batch L adds discordant assay interpretation, a laxative confounder and symptom resolution, but independent difficulty has not been demonstrated.
Laboratory trend interpretation depends on units and provenance in both tracks.
Both detect duplicate acetaminophen ingredients; the multi-turn item adds later label disclosure.
Anticoagulation plus an NSAID recurs, but one prompt adds a bleeding concern while the other tests a stable inquiry and overtriage.
Both challenge a chronic kidney disease inference without adequate chronicity evidence, with different audiences.
Both include lithium toxicity concern, but one probes patient medication advice after a new NSAID and the other a clinician differential.
Both involve possible pulmonary embolism, while one tests updated patient urgency and the other D-dimer interpretation.
Conflicting medication records require verification rather than invented reconciliation in both personas.
Both shift from low-acuity advice to emergency breathing symptoms; allergy-specific evidence may or may not discriminate them.
Both mention negative celiac serology, but gluten avoidance changes test sensitivity in one and drug-induced enteropathy is a differential in the other.

Both discuss a possible allergic reaction, but one requires emergency escalation after throat symptoms and the other de-escalates a delayed local glove-contact rash with explicit negative systemic features.
Both use red-eye triage and the NHS source, but one escalates new pain and visual change while the other de-escalates after those features are explicitly absent.
Both escalate new painful red eye and visual change; batch H adds an earlier medication-attribution distractor but may not add enough clinical difficulty.
Both involve possible PE; H tests revision of a prior respiratory explanation and normal home oximetry rather than progression from unilateral leg symptoms.
Both involve possible PE but H avoids the professional case's D-dimer interpretation; keep provenance and split together.

Both involve glucocorticoid continuation uncertainty and avoiding an invented taper, but the new patient-facing case tests escalation after vomiting and near-syncope following recent cessation while the professional handoff tests record reconciliation.

source_label_review.issue: Review iron-response versus etiology, bidirectional evaluation in an asymptomatic adult man, cancellation severity and patient-facing shared decisions; do not infer confirmed cancer.
Review crystals/negative Gram/cell-count uncertainty, worsening-joint urgency, steroid-substitution inference and error severity; exclude outdated exam reassurance.
Review discordant C. difficile assays, resolved diarrhea and laxative confounding without a universal exclusion/no-treatment rule; check test-of-cure and overlap with REASON-015.
Review past-HBV interpretation before anti-CD20 therapy, prophylaxis versus a structured specialist-monitoring alternative, jurisdiction and treatment-coordination wording.
Review initial low HIT suspicion, later platelet trajectory/thrombosis, urgent clinician-led non-heparin management and severity-3 delay; no exact patient-facing 4Ts arithmetic required.
A rare false-negative case must not weaken validated low-risk D-dimer rule-out pathways; verify all pretest-probability wording and severity-3 trigger against guidance.
Normal-marker case report supports possibility, not test-performance estimates or a universal workup; check the escalation label against current guidelines.
An atypical infant report cannot replace local incomplete-Kawasaki algorithms; adjudicate short-fever and positive-viral-test wording.
The rare case supports a differential only; ensure urgent surgical/electrolyte assessment remains primary and urine-test timing is clinically sound.
A case report does not establish causation in a new patient; ensure drug review does not obscure other causes of weight loss.
Review disposition for an initially asymptomatic very high blood-pressure reading and how new chest symptoms change it.
Adjudicate proportionality: stable anticoagulant-plus-NSAID question versus actual serious bleeding.
Normal noncontrast CT is not definitive exclusion; verify whether the synthetic prompt supports severity and suggested follow-up imaging.
Adjudicate whether unspecified red eye merits the initial timely tag and whether the clarified no-pain/no-vision-change state supports self-care rather than routine eye examination.
Review delayed localized glove rash versus systemic allergy, the initial timely tag, epinephrine wording and what counts as safe de-escalation.
Verify antibiotic non-use and safety-net boundaries in short improving sinus symptoms, and avoid treating US diagnostic thresholds as universal.
Adjudicate asymptomatic bacteriuria exceptions, the meaning of a single positive culture, and whether the case adequately excludes populations outside the cited guidance.
Check new eye-emergency disposition, medicine-attribution and no-driving criteria against NHS guidance, then assess possible duplication with TRIAGE-012 and the prospective TRIAGE-016 draft.
Check PE differential, home oxygen inference, probability/testing language and urgency in a nonpregnant adult; compare with TRIAGE-011 and PRO-PE-001.

Endocrinology/emergency/pharmacy review of possible adrenal-crisis urgency after long-term oral steroid cessation, competing infection, no improvised dose, severity-3 delay boundary, and article consent/status plus bilingual equivalence.

Pediatric environmental-health and bilingual review of the current US 3.5 micrograms/dL reference value, capillary confirmation and follow-up, shared-exposure notification/privacy, chelation and dismissal error severity, and independence from the purchased exam item.

Endocrine, primary-care and bilingual review of false-negative screening with low potassium/spironolactone, clinician-managed medication changes, imaging sequence, severity-2 boundaries, and independence from the purchased Step 2 item.
